title: Schedule Times Added Durations Then Rolled Hours
text: id: COMP-008 domain: math title: Schedule Times Added Durations Then Rolled Hours tags: time, schedule, minutes memory: A schedule answer once came out an hour off because I added minutes in my head while crossing an hour boundary. I wrote the durations as one total minute count, converted to hours and leftover minutes, then added hours first and leftover minutes second. When the leftover minutes crossed 60, I carried one more hour instead of compressing the clock. The clock stopped being slippery once minutes had their own line.

title: Printer Rate Became Per Printer Per Minute
text: id: COMP-005 domain: math title: Printer Rate Became Per Printer Per Minute tags: rates, printers, unit-rate memory: A printer problem became clear only when I found the per-printer-per-minute rate. Four printers and six minutes made a combined work window, not a single machine. I divided pages by printers and minutes, then rebuilt the new combined rate for the smaller printer group. I wrote the combined rate explicitly as printers times per-printer rate, with pages per minute beside it, before dividing pages by that rate. The final time carried minutes, not pages.

title: Money Problems Kept Cents To Two Decimal Places
text: id: COMP-019 domain: math title: Money Problems Kept Cents To Two Decimal Places tags: money, rounding, decimals memory: A money answer once looked close but failed because I rounded too early. I kept cents through the calculation and rounded only at the final bill. The tax, fee, credit, and tier amounts each got two decimal places. The final dollar amount became both readable and exact enough.
